inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for the quarter ended 2026-06-26 (10-Q Q3 FY2026, XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding = 293M); cover-page basic count 289.5M at 2026-07-20. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-charge it. Buybacks (FY25 $1,347M; 9M FY26 $1,348M) far exceed SBC (~$170M/yr) -- the excess is capital return funded out of the modelled FCF, value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back): FY2025 $149M; 9M FY2026 $130M, FY2026E $172M (9M + Q4 at Q3 run-rate). Cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement are not tagged separately in XBRL and TE publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line; immaterial (<0.1% of revenue) and not added.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026E: 9M actual $1,348M (XBRL PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock) + Q4 at the 9M pace. FY2025 actual $1,347M. Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.fy0_basis: FY2026E = 9M actual (Q1-Q3 FY26 revenue $14,573M) + Q4 guide ~$5,250M = $19,823M (+14.8%, ties to the ~15% reported-growth guide). reported_fcf $3,300M = 9M actual $2,171M (OCF $2,997M less net capex $826M) + Q4 ~$1,130M (FY25 Q4 was $1,150M). These two FY0 figures are estimates until the FY2026 10-K (due ~mid-Nov 2026) and should be replaced then.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> CoE 9.8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5%, 18% tax -> 3.7% after tax; market-value weights ~92% equity / 8% debt -> 9.3%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: auto cyclicality, China concentration and AI customer concentration are charged in the bear flows and the 20% bear weight, not in a rate premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost already sits inside operating expense (and therefore EBITDA); operating lease liabilities ($491M at FY25) are EXCLUDED from net debt. One treatment (B-equivalent), no double-charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests immaterial; flows are consolidated = attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: operating company, cyclical industrial -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). TE is a design-in connector/sensor manufacturer, not a financial, REIT or holdco; no prior valuation or memory entry exists, so this is the first model decision. BASE YEAR: FY2026E (9 months reported + guided Q4) rather than a mid-cycle revenue base. Reasons: (1) the fiscal year is ~97% complete and the revenue level is largely structural -- Richards Manufacturing (~$400M, closed Apr-25) is in the base and the AI data-center step-up (AI revenue tracking ~$2.4B CY26, $3B FY27 target pulled forward) is backed by >70% order growth and a 1.1x book-to-bill; (2) Transportation (half of sales) is NOT at a cyclical peak -- global light-vehicle production is flat-to-down, so FY26 is not a peak-volume year for the larger segment. What IS near-peak is the MARGIN (GAAP EBITDA + SBC ~26% vs a 2017-2024 range of ~20-24%), so the mid-cycle judgment is applied there: the base case fades margin to 25.5% and the bear case to ~23.5%, rather than capitalising the FY26 record. Interest income ($83M FY25) NOT stripped: TE is net-debt ($4.4B), so the strip rule does not apply and the flows are unlevered EBITDA-based anyway. EBITDA definition: GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC, i.e. restructuring (~$100M/yr, recurring at TE every year) is left IN as an operating cost. Pending Astrodyne TDI acquisition (~$1.4B cash, ~$250M sales, close expected by end CY2026): its revenue is inside the FY27 base growth rate, so its purchase price is deducted in equity_bridge. Pension deficit not separately bridged (not tagged in XBRL; modest vs $64B market cap) -- a known small omission.

equity_bridge.note: Agreed Jul-2026, ~$1.4B cash, close expected by end CY2026; its ~$250M sales (~1.3pp) is included in FY27 growth in all scenarios

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.2-6.1%) diverges >30% from owner-FCF CAGR (17.6-24.5%) and from EPS (-6.2% 3yr). Equity is depressed by ~$1-2B/yr of buybacks plus dividends (book value is not the compounding measure here, as with V); GAAP EPS is distorted by a FY24 tax benefit (EPS $10.40) and a ~$1B FY25 non-cash tax charge (EPS $6.20). FCF CAGRs start from a FY20/FY22 trough (FY22 working-capital build). Revenue 5yr CAGR (7.2%, FY20 COVID trough to FY25, includes Richards) is the selected anchor; it overstates the through-cycle organic rate (~4-6% per TE's business model).
historical_growth.notes: FY windows end FY2025 (last audited year). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC; SBC is 0.6-0.9% of revenue so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are within 1pp -- SBC is not funding the growth. EPS 5yr undefined (FY2020 GAAP loss of -$0.73 on goodwill impairment).

base.wc_capture_note: Trade NWC (AR $3,749M + inventory $3,027M - AP $2,409M at 2026-06-26) is ~21% of annualised sales; 9M FY26 OCF vs NI+D&A+SBC implies ~-14% capture on incremental revenue. Growth consumes cash.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY26E pre-SBC EBITDA ~26.0% (9M GAAP op income $2,898M + D&A $758M + SBC $130M on $14,573M). Held ~26% while the AI order book converts, then faded to 25.5% as a through-cycle level: assumes one ordinary auto/industrial down-year inside the horizon rather than perpetual peak margin.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A 5.2% of sales in 9M FY26 includes acquired-intangible amortisation (Richards); capex 5.7% 9M FY26 elevated by AI and Nantong capacity, normalising to 5.0% (FY17-25 range 4.3-6.7%).

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 revenue +9% (~7.5% organic plus ~1.3pp Astrodyne TDI): the AI cloud book (data and power connectivity, $3B target pulled ahead of FY27) and the 1.1x book-to-bill carry the first year, while Transportation grows a few points on electrification/ADAS content against flat global vehicle builds. Growth then glides from 7% to 3% as AI capex normalises and TE settles at its 4-6% organic business model plus bolt-ons. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin holds ~26% for two years and fades to a through-cycle 25.5%, i.e. FY26's record margin is not capitalised in perpetuity. TE stays the solid number two to Amphenol in AI interconnect -- shares the growth, does not win it outright.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI data-center connectivity keeps compounding well past the $3B target (power distribution and copper-in-rack hold up against optical), Industrial mix shift and Richards/Astrodyne power-grid adjacencies lift margin toward Amphenol-like levels (27.5% pre-SBC EBITDA), and auto content outperformance of 5-7 points over production continues via high-voltage EV/hybrid platforms and Chinese OEM export programs. Revenue +12%/+10%/+9% then decelerates to 3.5%; terminal growth 3% and a 17x cap reflect a higher-quality, more secular mix.
scenario_narratives.bear: Two of TE's axes break at once: a hyperscaler AI capex pause (or faster optical displacement of copper) stalls the fastest-growing piece of Industrial, and a China auto price war plus US-China tariff escalation hits the ~25% of sales and ~35% of auto revenue tied to China. FY27 +2% (Astrodyne only), FY28 -4%, with decremental margins taking pre-SBC EBITDA to 22.5% before recovering to a mid-cycle 23.5% (the 2017-2024 average band). Capex is cut to 4.8%. No solvency question -- net debt/EBITDA stays near 1x -- this is a cyclical earnings reset and a de-rating to a 13x cap, not a broken franchise.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): two concentrated exposures -- a handful of hyperscale AI customers and China auto -- can turn simultaneously and the margin is at a record, so the down-cycle is more than a tail. Base 50%: guided FY26 and the order book make the near-term path well-evidenced. Bull 30% (below 35%): the bull case needs AI to keep compounding AND margin to close the gap to Amphenol AND auto content to keep outrunning a weak production backdrop -- several independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF on a FY2026E base year (9 months reported + guided Q4), with the cyclical normalisation applied to MARGIN rather than to revenue. FY26 revenue is mostly structural (acquired Richards sales, a design-in AI book backed by record orders) and Transportation is not at a volume peak, so rebasing revenue to a mid-cycle level would discard real, contracted growth. The record ~26% pre-SBC EBITDA margin, by contrast, is a peak-ish number for a business that ran 20-24% in 2017-2024, so the base fades it to 25.5% and the bear resets it to 23.5% after a FY28 downturn. Risk is charged once: a single 9.3% USD WACC across scenarios, with cyclicality and customer/China concentration expressed in the bear flows and a 20% bear weight. Terminal values use a 13-17x cap appropriate to a high-quality cyclical industrial; Gordon at 9.3%/2.5% is ~15x, so the base cap and Gordon nearly coincide.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI data-center demand concentrated in a few hyperscalers; a capex pause or optical-over-copper shift would hit the fastest-growing, highest-margin revenue
China: ~25% of sales and ~35% of auto revenue, exposed to the domestic auto price war and US-China tariffs
Margin is at a record; the base still assumes ~25.5% pre-SBC EBITDA through the cycle versus 20-24% historically
Share loss to Amphenol in AI interconnect, where it has out-executed on growth, margin and M&A
Bolt-on M&A cadence (Richards $2.3B, Astrodyne $1.4B) raises integration and capital-allocation risk; acquired growth is only value-creating if bought below the 9.3% WACC
FY0 revenue and FCF are guided/estimated until the FY2026 10-K (~mid-Nov 2026); pension deficit not bridged
